programme.title: Na Clangairean
programme.desc: Tha a’ Chearc Iarrainn ’son dannsa còmhla ri na Clangairean ach cho do thuig i gun robh dannsa cho doirbh! Saoil an dèan i chùis air? The Iron Chicken wants to dance with the Clangers, but she didn’t realise dancing was so difficult! Will she manage it?

programme.title: Na Clangairean
programme.desc: Nuair tha na Clangairean air planaid annasach ùr a lorg, tha ’ad 'son dèanamh beagan rannsachaidh. An dèidh dhaibh a dhol air chall, tha 'ad fortanach g' eil Granaidh faisg air làimh 'son an sàbhaladh. When the Clangers find a fascinating new planet, they do a little exploring. When they go astray, it’s lucky that Granny is nearby to save them.

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Tha Otto a feuchainn ri toirt air Oona gun a bhith cho eagallach mun dorchadas 's e ga brosnachadh a dhol chun na traghad le fhèin... tron oidhche! Otto attempts to help Oona get over a fear of the dark by encouraging her to take a special trip to the beach by herself... a night-time trip!

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Tha i air a bhith sileadh gu trom air a chreag 's a-nis tha poll anns gach àit'! Tha Mama airson 's gun cùm Oona sùil air Baba 's gun cùm i glan e - obair dhùbhlanach 's Baba airson leum 's na loin 's coimhead sna lochain! It has been raining heavily on the rock and now there's mud everywhere. Mama has asked Oona to watch Baba and to keep him nice and clean - a big challenge, as Baba wants to jump in muddy puddles and investigate the pond life.

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Tha an latha fìor theth ‘s tha Bing ‘s Flop a ceannach reòiteag son iad fhèin a chumail fionnar. Ge-tà, mus faigh iad air na reòiteagan ithe, tha aoidh annasach a nochdadh a tha feumach air beagan taic bhuapa...! It’s a very hot day and Bing and Flop have bought themselves ice lollies to help keep them cool. However, an unexpected guest in need of some help distracts them from their treats before they manage to eat them!

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Abair g’ eil deagh spòrs a’ dol ‘s Bing ‘s Sula a’ peantadh dealbh-balla còmhla. Ge-tà, tha trioblaid ag èirigh nuair a thig dathan bhon dealbh aig Bing am measg an dealbh a tha Sula air a chruthachadh...! Great fun is had at Ama’s crèche as Bing and Sula create their own mural. However, things get a bit fraught when paint from Bing’s rainbow picture runs into the tree that Sula was carefully creating!

programme.title: Peicein/Petit
programme.desc: Tha Peicein toilichte prìomh phàirt dealbh-chluich na sgoile fhaighinn, gus an cluinn e gur e “Bana-phrionnsa Bhàlaigh” an dealbh-chluich aca. Chan eil e airson a bhith na bhana-phrionnsa, oir ’s e nighean a tha sin! Petit is happy to be the star of the school play, until he discovers that the play they must act is 'The Brave Princess'. He doesn't want to be a princess, he's not a girl!

programme.title: Hilda
programme.desc: Tha Hilda, Mam is Twig a’ feuchainn rin slìghe a dhèanamh a-mach à coille neònach, far a bheil an t-uamhas fhrìdean is mòran chunnartan - is tha Flòraidh is Daibhidh cho làn iomagain air an son ‘s gu bheil ’ad a’ dol gan lorg. Hilda, her mum and Twig try to make their way out of a strange forest, full of trolls and much danger - while a worried David and Frida journey out of Trolberg to find them.

programme.title: An Sgoil
programme.desc: Tha sinn air ais ann an Sgoil Taobh na Cloiche airson teirm ùr. Tha tòrr air tachairt thairis air na saor-làithean. Cha robh an là in-sheirbheis cho soirbheachail `s a bha Maighstir Mackle an dùil agus tha Ms Sharpe air nochdadh sna pàipearan-naidheachd ri linn ‘s na thachair aig a’ Mhòd. Our cameras are back at Sgoil Taobh na Cloiche for a new term. A lot has happened over the holidays. The in-service day wasn’t as successful as Mr Mackle had hoped and Ms Sharpe has made the newspapers after what happened at the Mòd.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Seachd Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach seachdainn le sgioba-naidheachd BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Alleluia!
programme.desc: Iain MacKinnon reads excerpts from Gliocas bhon Bhìoball by Donald Saunders, and Mairi MacInnes narrates from The Mother’s Catechism.

programme.title: Dealbhan Fraoich/Heather's Portraits
programme.desc: Heather travels to South Uist where she meets Father Colin MacInnes. A priest for over 50 years, Father Colin spent over three decades working among the people of Ecuador. There he helped transform a hillside shanty town on the outskirts of Quito into a thriving community with a hospital, banks, schools and churches. Tha Fraoch Nic an Deòir a Ìle air ais air an sgrion le sreath ùr de “Dhealbhan Fraoich”. An dà chuid na tè-ealain agus na ceasnaiche, tha i a’dèanamh dealbhan dathte de Ghàidheil air a bheil sinn eòlach – agus a’tàladh asta iomadh sgeul mu eachdraidh am beatha. Sa phrògram seo, tha Fraoch a’siubhal a dh’Uibhist a Deas gus coinneachadh ri Maighstir Cailean MacAonghais. Tha esan air a bhi na shagart fad còrr is lethcheud bliadhna. Chuir e seachad barrachd air deich bliadhna fichead ag obair còmhla ri muinntir Ecuador: gu ìre is gun do chuidich e gus coimhearsnachd thruagh aig oir prìomh bhaile Quito a thoirt air adhart gu bhi na àite soirbheachail le ospadal, sgoiltean, eaglaisean is bancaichean. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Garradh Phadruig
programme.desc: Peter is busy planting in the garden and helps two budding gardeners with a pumpkin. Tha Pàdruig trang a’cur sa ghàrradh, agus a’cuideachadh dithis òga a’cur pheapaig.

programme.title: Miann na Maighdinn-mara/Mermaid Tales
programme.desc: Kate travels around the North End of Skye, visiting a castle with strong connections to Clan MacLeod.

programme.title: Rudan Beaga Bòidheach/Life’s Little Things
programme.desc: Tha Niamh dèidheil air a bhith a’ ruith agus tha eacarsaich na pàirt chudromach dha a beatha. Niamh loves running and being active is a big part of her life.

programme.title: Cuirm aig Celtic
programme.desc: Cuirm shònraichte bho Sian aig Celtic Connections gus an dàrna clàr aca a chomharrachadh. Anns a’ buidheann Ghàidhlig Albannach, tha triùir dhen na seinneadairean Gàidhlig as fheàrr – Eilidh NicCarmaig, Ceitlin Lilidh & Ellen NicDhòmhnaill – le luchd-ciùil eile nan cois gus an clàr aca a thaisbeanadh beò ann an dòigh nach cualas roimhe. Le taic bho Bon Débarras. Air a chlàradh aig Talla Barony. Sian perform an exclusive concert at Celtic Connections to celebrate the release of their second album. The Scottish Gaelic folk group comprises three of today’s top Gaelic singers – Eilidh Cormack, Ceitlin Lilidh and Ellen MacDonald – who are joined by an extended line-up of musicians to perform the album live as never before. Support comes from Bon Débarras. Recorded at The Barony Hall. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Na Sgiobairean mu Dheireadh/The Last Captains
programme.desc: Tha dubhadh na grèine a’ cur sgleò air a’ Chamas agus air fortan nan sgiobair – tha iad a’ ruith a-mach à connadh, tha na clèibh aotrom agus chan eil càil a’ gabhail mar bu chòir. A solar eclipse darkens the Gulf and the captains’ fortunes - fuel is low, traps are light, and nothing’s biting like it should. Dubbed in Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Samhradh air Sàl
programme.desc: Katie MacRitchie from Harris joins Angus Mackay to go fishing on a moody, misty summer's morning off the east coast of Lewis. Watched closely by a golden eagle, they fish for mackerel as the sun gradually emerges and chat about the role that fishing plays in the community life of the islands. Tha Katie NicRisnidh às na Hearadh còmhla ri Aonghas MacAoidh agus iad ag iasgach air madainn shamhraidh ghruamach, cheòthach far costa an ear Leòdhais. Tha iad ag iasgach airson rionnach, le iolaire-bhuidhe gan coimhead, fhad ’s a nochdas a’ ghrian mean air mhean agus iad a’ bruidhinn mun àite a th’ aig iasgach ann am beatha coimhearsnachd nan h-eileanan.

programme.title: Seo BBC ALBA. This is BBC ALBA
programme.desc: Sealladh ùr bho Alba. A new view from Scotland.

programme.title: The Last Battle of the Vikings
programme.desc: Nowhere in the British Isles was the Viking connection longer-lasting or deeper than in Scotland. Hundreds of years after their first hit-and-run raids, the Norsemen still dominated huge swathes of the country. But storm clouds were gathering. In 1263 the Norwegian king Haakon IV assembled a fleet of 120 longships to counter Scottish raids on the Norse Hebrides. It was a force comparable in size to the Spanish Armada over three centuries later. But like the Armada, the Norse fleet was eventually defeated by a powerful storm. Driven ashore near present-day Largs, the beleaguered Norsemen were attacked by a Scottish army. The outcome of this vicious encounter would mark the beginning of the end of Norse power in Scotland. Marine archaeologist Dr Jon Henderson tells the incredible story of the Norsemen in Scotland. Visiting fascinating archaeological sites across Scotland and Norway, he reveals that, although the battle at Largs marked the end of an era for the Norsemen, their presence continued to shape the identity and culture of the Scottish nation to the present day.

programme.title: Life on Earth
programme.desc: David Attenborough looks at the role of a few of the millions of insect species, some of which have developed extremely close relationships with plants. Insects pollinate flowers and in some cases neither flower nor insect can survive without the other.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Beginning at London Marylebone, the last great Victorian railway terminus to be built in the capital, Michael Portillo embarks on a postwar exploration of Britain’s southern counties. He travels to Denham in Buckinghamshire, where engineers are constructing a striking new viaduct, High Wycombe, a historic centre of furniture-making thanks to its abundant of beechwood forest, and Oxford, where he discovers the postwar origins of the charity shop. In the Wiltshire countryside, Michael meets the head of the Soil Association and some of her saddleback piglets to hear how the organic movement was founded after the Second World War in reaction to the intensification of farming.

programme.title: Women's Test Cricket
programme.desc: Highlights of day three of the Lord's Test match between England Women and India Women.

programme.title: BBC Proms
programme.desc: From the 2016 BBC Proms, Martha Argerich performs Schubert's Rondo in A.

programme.title: Summer Night Concert from Vienna
programme.desc: The Vienna Philharmonic once again take up residency at the Schönbrunn Palace to bring us their annual Summer Night Concert. Set in the picturesque gardens, this concert is a staple of the classical music calendar. For the first time, the orchestra welcomes rising star Lorenzo Viotti as guest conductor – one of the most exciting young conductors on the scene. Joining them for this special evening is Welsh bass-baritone Sir Bryn Terfel, whose relationship with the orchestra spans many decades. He brings us arias from Verdi’s Falstaff, Wagner’s Das Rheingold along with Tevye’s song from the musical Fiddler on the Roof. Projected onto the façade of the Schönbrunn Palace, dancers from the Vienna State Ballet join the orchestra to bring the story of Daphnis and Chloé to life through the power of Ravel’s music. With music from the worlds of opera, musicals and ballet, together with symphonic works, this concert is a joyous musical summer treat.

programme.title: The Lark Ascending
programme.desc: Dame Diana Rigg explores the enduring popularity of The Lark Ascending by the English composer Ralph Vaughan Williams, which was recently voted Britain's favourite piece of classical music by listeners to Desert Island Discs on BBC Radio 4. Composed at a key turning point in world history, The Lark Ascending represents music for all occasions. It is used in rites of passage such as births, deaths and marriages, and is a favourite for film-makers looking to create that quintessential English pastoral feel. Fans of the work include actor Peter Sallis, who wants a copy of The Lark Ascending to be buried with him, top violinist Tasmin Little, who has played the piece as part of the BBC Proms, and music critic Michael Kennedy, who was a personal friend of Vaughan Williams. The programme includes a beautiful new performance of the work in the same village hall where it was heard for the first time in December 1920. The Lark Ascending is performed by 15-year-old violin prodigy Julia Hwang and pianist Charles Matthews, using the original arrangement for violin and piano.

programme.title: Letters from Baghdad
programme.desc: The extraordinary and dramatic story of Gertrude Bell, the most powerful woman in the British Empire in her day. She shaped the modern Middle East after World War I in ways that still reverberate today. More influential than her friend and colleague Lawrence of Arabia, Bell helped draw the borders of Iraq and established the Iraq Museum. Using never-seen-before footage of the region, the film chronicles Bell's extraordinary journey into both the uncharted Arabian desert and the inner sanctum of British male colonial power. With unique access to documents from the Iraq National Library and Archive and Gertrude Bell's own 1,600 letters, the story is told entirely in the words of the players of the day, excerpted verbatim from intimate letters, private diaries and secret communiques. It is a unique look at both a remarkable woman and the tangled history of Iraq.

programme.title: The Man Who Discovered Egypt
programme.desc: Documentary about English Egyptologist Flinders Petrie, the pioneer of systematic methodology in archaeology. Ancient Egypt was vandalised by tomb raiders and treasure hunters until this Victorian adventurer took them on. Most people have never heard of him, but this maverick undertook a scientific survey of the pyramids, discovered the oldest portraits in the world, unearthed Egypt's prehistoric roots - and in the process invented modern field archaeology, giving meaning to a whole civilisation.

programme.title: Summer Night Concert from Vienna
programme.desc: The Vienna Philharmonic once again take up residency at the Schönbrunn Palace to bring us their annual Summer Night Concert. Set in the picturesque gardens, this concert is a staple of the classical music calendar. For the first time, the orchestra welcomes rising star Lorenzo Viotti as guest conductor – one of the most exciting young conductors on the scene. Joining them for this special evening is Welsh bass-baritone Sir Bryn Terfel, whose relationship with the orchestra spans many decades. He brings us arias from Verdi’s Falstaff, Wagner’s Das Rheingold along with Tevye’s song from the musical Fiddler on the Roof. Projected onto the façade of the Schönbrunn Palace, dancers from the Vienna State Ballet join the orchestra to bring the story of Daphnis and Chloé to life through the power of Ravel’s music. With music from the worlds of opera, musicals and ballet, together with symphonic works, this concert is a joyous musical summer treat.

programme.title: The Last Battle of the Vikings
programme.desc: Nowhere in the British Isles was the Viking connection longer-lasting or deeper than in Scotland. Hundreds of years after their first hit-and-run raids, the Norsemen still dominated huge swathes of the country. But storm clouds were gathering. In 1263 the Norwegian king Haakon IV assembled a fleet of 120 longships to counter Scottish raids on the Norse Hebrides. It was a force comparable in size to the Spanish Armada over three centuries later. But like the Armada, the Norse fleet was eventually defeated by a powerful storm. Driven ashore near present-day Largs, the beleaguered Norsemen were attacked by a Scottish army. The outcome of this vicious encounter would mark the beginning of the end of Norse power in Scotland. Marine archaeologist Dr Jon Henderson tells the incredible story of the Norsemen in Scotland. Visiting fascinating archaeological sites across Scotland and Norway, he reveals that, although the battle at Largs marked the end of an era for the Norsemen, their presence continued to shape the identity and culture of the Scottish nation to the present day.

programme.title: Life on Earth
programme.desc: David Attenborough looks at the role of a few of the millions of insect species, some of which have developed extremely close relationships with plants. Insects pollinate flowers and in some cases neither flower nor insect can survive without the other.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Beginning at London Marylebone, the last great Victorian railway terminus to be built in the capital, Michael Portillo embarks on a postwar exploration of Britain’s southern counties. He travels to Denham in Buckinghamshire, where engineers are constructing a striking new viaduct, High Wycombe, a historic centre of furniture-making thanks to its abundant of beechwood forest, and Oxford, where he discovers the postwar origins of the charity shop. In the Wiltshire countryside, Michael meets the head of the Soil Association and some of her saddleback piglets to hear how the organic movement was founded after the Second World War in reaction to the intensification of farming.

programme.title: The Lark Ascending
programme.desc: Dame Diana Rigg explores the enduring popularity of The Lark Ascending by the English composer Ralph Vaughan Williams, which was recently voted Britain's favourite piece of classical music by listeners to Desert Island Discs on BBC Radio 4. Composed at a key turning point in world history, The Lark Ascending represents music for all occasions. It is used in rites of passage such as births, deaths and marriages, and is a favourite for film-makers looking to create that quintessential English pastoral feel. Fans of the work include actor Peter Sallis, who wants a copy of The Lark Ascending to be buried with him, top violinist Tasmin Little, who has played the piece as part of the BBC Proms, and music critic Michael Kennedy, who was a personal friend of Vaughan Williams. The programme includes a beautiful new performance of the work in the same village hall where it was heard for the first time in December 1920. The Lark Ascending is performed by 15-year-old violin prodigy Julia Hwang and pianist Charles Matthews, using the original arrangement for violin and piano.

programme.title: Letters from Baghdad
programme.desc: The extraordinary and dramatic story of Gertrude Bell, the most powerful woman in the British Empire in her day. She shaped the modern Middle East after World War I in ways that still reverberate today. More influential than her friend and colleague Lawrence of Arabia, Bell helped draw the borders of Iraq and established the Iraq Museum. Using never-seen-before footage of the region, the film chronicles Bell's extraordinary journey into both the uncharted Arabian desert and the inner sanctum of British male colonial power. With unique access to documents from the Iraq National Library and Archive and Gertrude Bell's own 1,600 letters, the story is told entirely in the words of the players of the day, excerpted verbatim from intimate letters, private diaries and secret communiques. It is a unique look at both a remarkable woman and the tangled history of Iraq.

programme.title: The Man Who Discovered Egypt
programme.desc: Documentary about English Egyptologist Flinders Petrie, the pioneer of systematic methodology in archaeology. Ancient Egypt was vandalised by tomb raiders and treasure hunters until this Victorian adventurer took them on. Most people have never heard of him, but this maverick undertook a scientific survey of the pyramids, discovered the oldest portraits in the world, unearthed Egypt's prehistoric roots - and in the process invented modern field archaeology, giving meaning to a whole civilisation.

programme.title: TechXplore
programme.desc: As football fever sweeps the globe, Paul Carter discovers how technology is transforming the beautiful game and leaving a legacy for future generations. Kicking off at Boston Dynamics, Paul meets the robots redefining matchday and goes up against 'robot Ronaldo'. In Philadelphia, he visits the university students using AI to unlock new levels of sporting performance. And at TOCA in California, he puts cutting-edge ball technology to the test, alongside the stars of tomorrow. From artists to innovators, join Paul as he meets the pioneering people shaping the future of football.

programme.title: What Happened at...?
programme.desc: On 1 July 1916, nearly 20,000 British soldiers were killed on the first day of the Battle of the Somme – one of the bloodiest days in the history of warfare and a lasting symbol of both sacrifice and futility. In this documentary, Jordan Dunbar examines how communities have been shaped by the battle and reveals how its legacy continues to resonate through families - including his own.

programme.title: Clive Myrie’s Caribbean Adventure
programme.desc: Clive visits the bustling district of Vedado, the most modern and affluent part of Havana. He takes a motorcycle tour with Ernesto Guevara, Che Guevara’s son, finds out how to create an amazing feast even though Cubans live under rationing, and stretches himself with a lesson in ballet at Carlos Acosta’s school. He also learns how to make the perfect Cuban cocktail.

programme.title: The Climate Question
programme.desc: A global programme that reflects the variety of takes on climate change, how best to understand it and the world's attempts to avert it, temper it or adapt to it. It is not about questioning whether climate change is happening, it's about finding the best ways to respond to it. This is sharp-edged, analytical inquiry. Hard scrutiny, touched with a sense of adventure and discovery, and where we can find it, hope. It includes stories from across the world on why we find it so hard to save our own planet, and how we might change that.

programme.title: China's Greatest Treasures
programme.desc: Dragon is the ultimate symbol of China. Chinese people often call themselves the descendants of the dragon. Unlike in western mythology where dragons are depicted as monsters to be tamed, in China, dragons are seen as life-giving, beneficent and auspicious. Once you know about them, you notice them everywhere in China. In this episode, Alastair explores the art of dragons, to understand how this mythical creature has become so ingrained in Chinese national identity.

programme.title: The Media Show
programme.desc: Nigel Farage has accused parts of the British media of mounting a politically-motivated campaign against him after reports about his financial interests prompted an investigation by Parliament's Standards Commissioner. Gabriel Pogrund, editor of the Insight investigations team at The Sunday Times, outlines the reporting behind their story, while journalist Michael Crick and Brendan O'Neill of Spiked discuss the political and journalistic issues. A High Court judgment has dismissed all claims brought by Prince Harry and six other claimants against Associated Newspapers over allegations that journalists used unlawful methods to obtain information. The ruling marks a significant moment in the long-running legal and political legacy of Britain's phone-hacking and press intrusion scandals. Susan Aslan, media lawyer, outlines the legal significance of the judgment.

programme.title: Asia
programme.desc: In the heart of Asia lie vast, arid lands. These deserts and dry grasslands are so hostile that they push life to the limit. Here, one of the rarest animals on earth, the Gobi bear, searches desperately for water, and the bizarre-looking long-eared jerboas use their striking features to catch prey. Asiatic lions must do whatever it takes to find food, and juvenile cormorants resort to cannibalism to survive. On the arid grasslands, Pallas cats need ingenious ways to get close to their prey, Mongolian gazelles must battle harsh winters and human barriers, and takhi are terrorised each night by Mongolian wolves. Life in the arid heart of Asia demands extraordinary resilience – those that live here are the continent's great survivors.

programme.title: Asia
programme.desc: In the heart of Asia lie vast, arid lands. These deserts and dry grasslands are so hostile that they push life to the limit. Here, one of the rarest animals on earth, the Gobi bear, searches desperately for water, and the bizarre-looking long-eared jerboas use their striking features to catch prey. Asiatic lions must do whatever it takes to find food, and juvenile cormorants resort to cannibalism to survive. On the arid grasslands, Pallas cats need ingenious ways to get close to their prey, Mongolian gazelles must battle harsh winters and human barriers, and takhi are terrorised each night by Mongolian wolves. Life in the arid heart of Asia demands extraordinary resilience – those that live here are the continent's great survivors.

programme.title: Asia
programme.desc: In the heart of Asia lie vast, arid lands. These deserts and dry grasslands are so hostile that they push life to the limit. Here, one of the rarest animals on earth, the Gobi bear, searches desperately for water, and the bizarre-looking long-eared jerboas use their striking features to catch prey. Asiatic lions must do whatever it takes to find food, and juvenile cormorants resort to cannibalism to survive. On the arid grasslands, Pallas cats need ingenious ways to get close to their prey, Mongolian gazelles must battle harsh winters and human barriers, and takhi are terrorised each night by Mongolian wolves. Life in the arid heart of Asia demands extraordinary resilience – those that live here are the continent's great survivors.

programme.title: Asia
programme.desc: In the heart of Asia lie vast, arid lands. These deserts and dry grasslands are so hostile that they push life to the limit. Here, one of the rarest animals on earth, the Gobi bear, searches desperately for water, and the bizarre-looking long-eared jerboas use their striking features to catch prey. Asiatic lions must do whatever it takes to find food, and juvenile cormorants resort to cannibalism to survive. On the arid grasslands, Pallas cats need ingenious ways to get close to their prey, Mongolian gazelles must battle harsh winters and human barriers, and takhi are terrorised each night by Mongolian wolves. Life in the arid heart of Asia demands extraordinary resilience – those that live here are the continent's great survivors.

programme.title: Asia
programme.desc: In the heart of Asia lie vast, arid lands. These deserts and dry grasslands are so hostile that they push life to the limit. Here, one of the rarest animals on earth, the Gobi bear, searches desperately for water, and the bizarre-looking long-eared jerboas use their striking features to catch prey. Asiatic lions must do whatever it takes to find food, and juvenile cormorants resort to cannibalism to survive. On the arid grasslands, Pallas cats need ingenious ways to get close to their prey, Mongolian gazelles must battle harsh winters and human barriers, and takhi are terrorised each night by Mongolian wolves. Life in the arid heart of Asia demands extraordinary resilience – those that live here are the continent's great survivors.

programme.title: Reporting Scotland
programme.desc: All the weekend national, UK-wide and international news on Sunday evening at 7.

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.desc: Dom steps inside Glasgow’s Britannia Panopticon, the world’s oldest surviving music hall, to help piano technician Jamie revive Henrietta, a 1904 Nilson pianola with roots in a New York speakeasy. Will is in Inverness to collect Debbi’s handcrafted chess set, a family heirloom that requires Kirsten’s expert touch if it is to be played with again. In Birnam, Dom is getting hands on with a craft that has remained unchanged for centuries as he masters steam bending and pine-tar finishing with Scotland’s only wooden ski maker.

programme.title: Island Crossings
programme.desc: Weather and mechanical issues cause havoc across the network, jeopardising thousands of pounds in fresh Barra shellfish, and there is a hotly contested oyster competition.

programme.title: Paramedics on Scene
programme.desc: In Ayr, crewmates Sophie and Shelby are called to a critical incident involving a woman who has suffered a burst gastric ulcer and is losing pints of blood. The team must act fast to take their patient to resus, the part of a hospital reserved for the most serious emergencies. Meanwhile, Aberdeen-based paramedic Andrew, technician Simon and student Matthew treat Patrick, who is displaying a range of worrying symptoms, including a worsening headache, a rash and a sensitivity to light. The team can’t rule out meningitis but encounter a queue of ambulances outside Aberdeen Royal Infirmary. As Patrick’s condition deteriorates, the crew must administer treatment in the back of the ambulance. In North Ayrshire, Pam and Robert of the Special Operations Response Team attend a road traffic collision involving mum Joanne and young daughter Iris. Robert has to treat the pair calmly and reassuringly as they cope with the immediate aftermath of the upsetting incident. And just outside Dundee, ambulance teammates Chloe and David are called to a local police station where a man is trying to calm himself after taking an overdose of base, a particularly potent form of crack cocaine.

programme.title: Still Game
programme.desc: When Jack and Victor aren't invited to the wedding of the year, they decide to do something about it. Meanwhile Winston has his own plan to get an invite.

programme.title: Scot Squad
programme.desc: Top comic capers from Caledonia's crack team of cops. Out in the sticks, an outbreak of dodgy merchandise on sale in rural pubs sees Charlie McIntosh and Jane Mackay going undercover - with a little help from an all-time music legend on a night off. Volunteer officer Ken Beattie shows up at a city centre van to receive soup, sustenance and key info on shady deals. The Chief discovers a whole new world of insults when he flexes his itchy trigger finger and samples online gaming, while Maggie Le Beau produces the perfect piece of equipment to cut short any pocket dial. Blue light spoof comedy starring Jack Docherty, Chris Forbes, Ashley Smith, James Allenby-Kirk, M L Stone with special guest Phil Cunningham.

programme.title: The Troops
programme.desc: Under fire in Estonia, HQ falls and Shep takes command. Back home, there are goodbyes, scars, and one final performance to mark the end of duty and the start of something new.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Anita Rani begins a four-part journey along England’s east coast, exploring the wildlife, landscapes and communities adapting to life on the edge of the sea. programme.title: Weatherman Walking
programme.desc: Derek Brockway revisits three wildlife walks. First, he braves the rain in Gwynedd, then hunts for water voles in Radnorshire and finally sees ancient rock formations in Ceredigion.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: George Anderson and Calum Clunie are back together to tackle the week’s jobs at Beechgrove Garden. Although George got a special picking of potatoes for his birthday in June, this is the time to lift the first crop from the vegetable plot and try out this year’s produce. Calum and George check on the brassicas that were planted in the club root-infected bed, testing varieties that are said to be resistant to the infection. George is back to work on the privet hedge that was given a severe pruning last year to encourage thicker growth, Calum gets round to placing plants known for their fragrance in his competition bed, and there are the week’s handy hints.

programme.title: This Wild Life
programme.desc: Wildlife expert Saba Douglas-Hamilton, together with her husband Frank and their three young children, move to the romantic Samburu National Reserve in Kenya to run a safari camp for the first time. But life out there isn't easy. There are monkeys in the kitchen, floods threatening the camp and, with no fences to keep out the wildlife, elephants are regular house guests. This series follows their ups and downs as the family struggles to keep guests, elephants, lions and even crocodiles smiling. The family is settling into their new life running a safari camp and protecting elephants in northern Kenya's remote Samburu National Reserve. Guests have arrived and are expecting a luxury wildlife experience, but Saba is called away to rescue an injured crocodile. And the camp team comes face to face with a bull elephant in a dramatic search for a young child lost in the bush. It's a nail-biting adventure for Saba and her warrior friends.

programme.title: Talking Tennis
programme.desc: Tennis addict Alistair McGowan serves up an affectionate look back at one of the world's greatest tournaments - Wimbledon. Here, he is focusing on the game's greatest rivalries and the big battles - physical and mental - that have been fought over the years on the lawns of SW19 and helped turn two weeks of British summertime into our favourite gladiatorial spectacle. Featuring classic interviews and rarely seen footage from the BBC's archives, this episode examines the confrontations between Evert and Navratilova, Ashe and Connors, Borg and McEnroe, Graf and Seles, and Sampras and Agassi - as well as the more recent rivalries between the Williams sisters, Federer, Nadal and Djokovik. It also looks at the tactics players can use to triumph as they push each other to the limit - mind games, tantrums and the fine art of grunting.

programme.title: Wimbledon
programme.desc: Live coverage of the Championships at the All England Lawn Tennis Club at Wimbledon.

programme.title: Andi Oliver’s Fabulous Feasts
programme.desc: In her old neighbourhood of Notting Hill, in west London, Andi Oliver revisits the past with her daughter Miquita to create her most fabulous feast yet, celebrating those doing incredible work to uplift the community. When she was in her early 20s, Andi raised her daughter in W10, and she wants to see if the community spirit she remembers from back in the day still exists here. For Andi and her daughter, it’s an emotional return to the familiar streets, meeting individuals working tirelessly to help those who need support. If she’s to do them justice, Andi needs to create an unforgettable feast that draws on the cultures that had a huge impact on her time here, particularly from the Caribbean and Morocco. At least she has a spectacular setting in mind for her party – the iconic Grade II listed block Trellick Tower. Can Andi pull together the ultimate block party with incredible music and unforgettable food that does justice to the place she once called home?

programme.title: Sweet Charity
programme.desc: Musical comedy about the romantic ups and downs of a dance partner-for-hire at a seedy New York dance hall, who longs for true love but has bad luck with men.

programme.title: Pride and Prejudice
programme.desc: The Bennet family of Longbourn are delighted to learn of the occupancy of nearby Netherfield Park by Charles Bingley, a wealthy young bachelor. Bingley develops an interest in Jane, the eldest of the five unmarried Bennet girls, but her sister Elizabeth is far from impressed by Bingley's haughty companion Mr Darcy.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: A collection of the best finds from the show's travels around the country.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: The next stop on Anita's road trip is West Mersea in Essex. While the county may be known for engineering and car manufacturing, along its coastline one industry has a much longer history. Oysters have been harvested here for more than 2,000 years, cultivated in the creeks around Mersea Island. Over the decades, oyster farming has adapted to changing environmental conditions and the arrival of the non-native Pacific rock oyster. To experience what oyster harvesting is like today, Anita heads onto the brackish waters to meet the people farming oysters. She also meets the team investigating how the non-native Pacific rock oyster is affecting the local ecosystem and whether it could play a role in helping coastal habitats respond to rising sea levels. Along the way, Anita looks back through the Countryfile archives at the people and projects shaping life around our coastline.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Antiques Roadshow comes from the beautiful grounds of the imposing Elizabethan mansion Wollaton Hall in Nottingham. Silver expert Kate Flitcroft is shaken, not stirred, by a stunning fire extinguisher cocktail shaker that turns up, while ceramics expert Eric Knowles meets his match with a cheeky toy monkey popping out of a musical pineapple. Fiona Bruce arrives in style on an iconic Chopper bike and tells the story of Raleigh Bicycles, founded in Nottingham in the 1880s. She learns about local activist George Powe, who campaigned to secure employment opportunities for black workers at Raleigh in the 1950s, and hears from two former employees about life inside what was once the world’s largest bicycle factory. Jewellery expert Susan Rumfitt challenges Fiona to guess the value of three intriguing cameo items, and collectables expert Hilary Kay is surprised to discover some of Queen Victoria’s personal undergarments with a sizeable price tag to boot.

programme.title: The Tech Billionaire Takeover
programme.desc: A new generation of tech billionaires believe their technologies can replace democracy as we know it and upend the global financial system. Matt Shea gets inside access to this new super-elite, visiting the sovereign nations they're building and tracing their growing political connections to the Trump administration. Are these men trying to take over the world?

programme.title: Oppenheimer
programme.desc: The life of J Robert Oppenheimer, the physicist appointed by the US to run the Manhattan Project, their bid to develop the atomic bomb before the Nazis. Brilliant as he is, winning that race comes at a cost, and amidst his guilt and grief at what he's done, he is also suspected by the authorities of being a communist spy.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Anita Rani begins a four-part journey along England’s east coast, exploring the wildlife, landscapes and communities adapting to life on the edge of the sea. Her first stop is Northey Island in Essex, an internationally important refuge for threatened birds, including curlew, lapwing and dunlin. With rising sea levels putting increasing pressure on coastal habitats, Anita discovers an innovative conservation project using retired Thames barges to help protect the island’s future. She also meets the volunteers working to safeguard vulnerable ringed plover nests using a simple but effective solution. Anita also delves into the Countryfile archives to revisit some of the projects helping to create more space for nature to thrive.

programme.title: Weatherman Walking
programme.desc: Derek Brockway revisits three wildlife walks. First, he braves the rain in Gwynedd, then hunts for water voles in Radnorshire and finally sees ancient rock formations in Ceredigion.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: George Anderson and Calum Clunie are back together to tackle the week’s jobs at Beechgrove Garden. Although George got a special picking of potatoes for his birthday in June, this is the time to lift the first crop from the vegetable plot and try out this year’s produce. Calum and George check on the brassicas that were planted in the club root-infected bed, testing varieties that are said to be resistant to the infection. George is back to work on the privet hedge that was given a severe pruning last year to encourage thicker growth, Calum gets round to placing plants known for their fragrance in his competition bed, and there are the week’s handy hints.

programme.title: This Wild Life
programme.desc: Wildlife expert Saba Douglas-Hamilton, together with her husband Frank and their three young children, move to the romantic Samburu National Reserve in Kenya to run a safari camp for the first time. But life out there isn't easy. There are monkeys in the kitchen, floods threatening the camp and, with no fences to keep out the wildlife, elephants are regular house guests. This series follows their ups and downs as the family struggles to keep guests, elephants, lions and even crocodiles smiling. The family is settling into their new life running a safari camp and protecting elephants in northern Kenya's remote Samburu National Reserve. Guests have arrived and are expecting a luxury wildlife experience, but Saba is called away to rescue an injured crocodile. And the camp team comes face to face with a bull elephant in a dramatic search for a young child lost in the bush. It's a nail-biting adventure for Saba and her warrior friends.

programme.title: Talking Tennis
programme.desc: Tennis addict Alistair McGowan serves up an affectionate look back at one of the world's greatest tournaments - Wimbledon. Here, he is focusing on the game's greatest rivalries and the big battles - physical and mental - that have been fought over the years on the lawns of SW19 and helped turn two weeks of British summertime into our favourite gladiatorial spectacle. Featuring classic interviews and rarely seen footage from the BBC's archives, this episode examines the confrontations between Evert and Navratilova, Ashe and Connors, Borg and McEnroe, Graf and Seles, and Sampras and Agassi - as well as the more recent rivalries between the Williams sisters, Federer, Nadal and Djokovik. It also looks at the tactics players can use to triumph as they push each other to the limit - mind games, tantrums and the fine art of grunting.

programme.title: Wimbledon

programme.title: Andi Oliver’s Fabulous Feasts
programme.desc: In her old neighbourhood of Notting Hill, in west London, Andi Oliver revisits the past with her daughter Miquita to create her most fabulous feast yet, celebrating those doing incredible work to uplift the community. When she was in her early 20s, Andi raised her daughter in W10, and she wants to see if the community spirit she remembers from back in the day still exists here. For Andi and her daughter, it’s an emotional return to the familiar streets, meeting individuals working tirelessly to help those who need support. If she’s to do them justice, Andi needs to create an unforgettable feast that draws on the cultures that had a huge impact on her time here, particularly from the Caribbean and Morocco. At least she has a spectacular setting in mind for her party – the iconic Grade II listed block Trellick Tower. Can Andi pull together the ultimate block party with incredible music and unforgettable food that does justice to the place she once called home?

programme.title: Cooking Buddies
programme.desc: Get your dancing shoes ready because Buddy and Conker get a call from Jaylen, a young salsa dancer who doesn’t stop moving! His mum is a professional salsa dancer, and Jaylen has learned all his moves from her, as he loves connecting with their Colombian roots through dancing. But there’s one thing that Jaylen loves even more... eggs! He asks Buddy to teach him an egg-cellent meal that he can make for his family. Buddy knows that if Jaylen loves dancing salsa, then he has to get him making salsa too, so he comes up with a cracking egg tortilla wrap filled with guacamole and zingy salsa. They learn to make their own tortilla dough in minutes, an omelette that sticks to the tortilla in the pan and colourful tomato salsa and creamy guacamole – cracking! Jaylen’s keen to get Buddy learning his kind of salsa too, so Buddy learns the basics of posture and footwork with the help of Jaylen… and some colourful socks! Join Buddy, Conker and Jaylen in this episode of Cooking Buddies that gets salsa onto your plate and into your step. You can get all of Buddy’s recipes, and loads more, at bbc.co.uk/food

programme.title: Zog

programme.title: Piripenguins

programme.title: Rafi the Wishing Wizard
programme.desc: At the playground, Khia won’t let Rafi and Ruby have a turn on the zip line. Rafi makes a wish for a magical new zip line that loops through the clouds and zooms around the park. At first, it’s amazing. But Rafi and Ruby ride again and again, forgetting the rule of one turn each. Soon, a long queue forms, and the friends realise they’re doing exactly what Khia did. Rafi decides it’s time to let others have a go. She realises that playground fun works best when everyone gets a turn.

programme.title: Big Lizard
programme.desc: When a pack of pesky, migrating trilobites overrun the ship, Big Lizard has to use a hidden talent to lure them away. But one little trilobite, Rex, decides to stay.

programme.title: Spidey and His Amazing Friends
programme.desc: Spidey teams up with Thing. Spidey's tech is taken.

programme.title: Knee High Spies
programme.desc: Silver Paw invades the playhouse. Jeremy and Deena must stop it from becoming her lair.

programme.title: The Weasy Family
programme.desc: The ducklings can't get their pop's attention - he spends all his time playing on his phone! They force him outside to play ball, but Weasy is obsessed. The ducklings decide to confiscate the phone, but Weasy has no intention of giving in.

programme.title: Talking Tom Heroes: Suddenly Super
programme.desc: Ginger discovers the Peak City Heroes' big secret.

programme.title: Monster Makes

The Recycling Express brings an empty box, which Rebecca and Murphi transform into a cardboard kitty cat.

programme.title: My World Kitchen
programme.desc: Je'nae is cooking her favourite meal of Jamaican saltfish and cabbage. Her family are Jamaican, and in Jamaica saltfish and cabbage is a very popular meal. Lots of people eat it for their breakfast, but Je'nae is cooking it as a very special dinner for her friends. She is using saltfish, fresh cabbage and colourful peppers in her meal. Je'nae's friends have mixed opinions about the taste of fresh green pepper. She hopes that they will like it cooked in her recipe. Her mum has cooked some tasty Jamaican dumplings and rice to eat with the fish, and Je'nae is really looking forward to seeing if her friends will like it as much as she does.

programme.title: Hamza Loves Animals: Africa
programme.desc: Kipekee the baby elephant and her friends find ways to cool down in the hot sun. Hamza sees vultures in the wild, and some of the animals get weighed at the orphanage.

programme.title: Down on the Farm
programme.desc: Storm visits a farm in Warwickshire to find out all about some unusual animals - buffalo. JB goes to a rooftop farm in the city to discover how fish help to grow salad leaves and herbs. Some school children in London show Storm how to make compost with some very helpful creatures. JB shares a spring poem and we see how potatoes are planted on a farm in Scotland.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: It's Evie and Doug's first playdate together with their friends. They try out their new ball pit, but Waffle can't join in because he's not toilet trained. He finds fun elsewhere.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Duggee is cleaning the clubhouse, so the Squirrels take refuge in the treehouse, but it's getting a little bit cramped these days. Norrie has an idea - maybe they need to add an extension, just like her dad does when she gets new siblings.

programme.title: Octonauts
programme.desc: The Octonauts roam the oceans in search of adventure and fun. When the Octopod breaks down, Tweak and the crew search for a missing part aboard an abandoned prototype of the ship, not realising something lives there.

programme.title: Vida the Vet
programme.desc: Vida and Popcorn's search for a mysterious stink in the koala family home leads to young Pippen receiving a much-needed lesson in flossing.

programme.title: Go Jetters
programme.desc: Grandmaster Glitch demands the Grimbots find somewhere with no cars so he can practice riding his bike without stabilisers. He arrives in Venice and is delighted to find the 'streets' are empty. With a splash, he discovers there are no cars because there are no streets in this city of canals and demands the Grimbots build him some roads. The Go Jetters and other tourists now find their gondola rides blocked by roads and concrete.

programme.title: Big Lizard
programme.desc: Dad drops an essential gizmo in a hard-to-reach place. Big Lizard takes them on an underwater adventure to meet Ammon, the tentacled solution to their problem!

programme.title: Yukee
programme.desc: Stripes has borrowed Twinkle's xylophone, but he has lost it - and right before her performance! The gang race around the garden, listening for clues. But will they find it in time?

programme.title: Froglets
programme.desc: Ziff, Pipp and Button get creative with empty toilet rolls and turn into Froggie robots.

programme.title: Mr Tumble
programme.desc: It’s time to sing and sign along with Mr Tumble! Sing and sign along with Mr Tumble about being brave, friends, sharing and manners.

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Ben meets Gabe at the park for some den building and hide-and-seek. Mr Tumble and Grandad are playing hide-and-seek too - by mistake! There is a treasure hunt in the spotty surprise. Featuring signs for the words tree, hiding and magnifying glass.

programme.title: Dog Squad
programme.desc: Dan the border collie is a search and rescue dog who works with his owner Jamie. His super nose follows scents and smells so they can rescue people who need their help. A local artist is painting the view of Woofton from a hill. But when the wind gets too strong, he gets lost on his way down. Dan and Jamie are called to try to find him. Dan finds the artist's scent, leading him to his painting. Jamie recognises the scene and takes the lead, but the weather is getting worse. Can Dan's super nose lead them to the artist in time?

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: Ginger and the Peas embark on an underground chase in pursuit of a burrowing Aritchokus.

programme.title: Zog
programme.desc: Zog and the doctors do their best to care for Twiggy until his demands become too much. Once they realise what is really wrong, they help Twiggy feel special again.

programme.title: The Game Catchers
programme.desc: The Game Catchers are a team of five friends on an interstellar journey to explore fantastic planets, with the aim of learning about and playing new games. The discovered games are collected into a database to make sure they are never lost.

programme.title: Roots and Fruits
programme.desc: Live from the Roots and Fruits theatre, it’s the fabulous Avocados singing an operatic piece in their three unique voices!

programme.title: Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Oona, Baba and May visit Mossy in the Undergrowth. They discover that a mysterious visitor has been sleeping in his den - and everyone else's dens too! When Oona spots a clue, the friends set out to follow the trail and investigate. Can Detective Oona solve the case and find the culprit?

programme.title: Numberblocks
programme.desc: The toys in Numberblock Five's new toy library are all mixed up! How can Numberblock Two find something to play with? Luckily, their new friend, Sorty the Super Sorter, helps them discover that toys can be sorted by type, colour, shape and size. It’s easy to see them all and find the perfect toy when they are sorted neatly into categories.

programme.title: Colourblocks
programme.desc: Green stages a magic show to introduce her new friends Black and White. Learn the difference between light, bright and dark colours with the Colourblocks.

programme.title: Froglets
programme.desc: The Froglets find a magnifying glass and become detectives to hunt for a missing crayon.

programme.title: Monster Makes
programme.desc: It's picnic day! Rebecca and Murphi create a 'soup-er' fly in a bowl of soup. On the Recycling Express, an old storage tub becomes a totally terrific tub drum kit.

programme.title: Go Wild
programme.desc: Steve and Aneeshwar meet some agile gibbons who show them how well they can move. Though the gibbons are a little quiet, Steve and Aneeshwar have a go at showing what they sound like in the wild. Next, they meet a tall, long-legged bird called a seriema who is very interested in a pretend toy snake, before they reveal the unusual wild connection between the two animals.

programme.title: Playtime Towers
programme.desc: It’s party time in Playtime Towers, and Bella and Lift enjoy a wibbly-wobbly jelly treat. Over in Boxtropolis, this gives Sketch an idea to paint a jellyfish.

programme.title: Yukee
programme.desc: As everyone huddles in Sonny’s caravan during a storm, Toad admits he’s frightened of the sound. Can Yukee find a way to use the pitter-pitter-pitter-patter of the rain to calm him?

programme.title: Tiny Tunes
programme.desc: Lisa and the children paint calming mobiles, learning British Sign Language signs for mama, buy and cry, then sing and sign Hush Little Baby Don’t You Cry.

programme.title: Nick Cope's Popcast
programme.desc: A scaly little visitor gives Nick and Norman an idea for today’s Popcast Song.

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: Ginger and the baby Pea-Rexes search for honeysuckles, leaving behind a trail of berries.

programme.title: Piripenguins
programme.desc: A sales rep visits. Despite Pancake’s doubts, he convinces the Piris to buy extra flippers. The penguins discover that their purchases are duds but find a clever new use for them.

programme.title: Zog
programme.desc: The doctors visit Fifi and see that she is feeling sad because her pies aren’t up to her usual standard. They take her out to cheer her up - until Zog realises what she really needs.

programme.title: Rafi the Wishing Wizard
programme.desc: Rafi and Finn find a lost baby sparrow in the park. Wanting to help, Rafi wishes she could talk to animals. Suddenly, ants, squirrels and Teacup the dog begin to chatter at once, making things more confusing! Rafi realises that listening can be more important than talking. She and Finn close their eyes and hear the sparrow’s mummy calling. Guided by the sound, they find the nest and reunite the chick with its family.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Jack’s the new dog at school and the newest recruit in Rusty’s army. Jack struggles with following instructions and always forgets his hat, but Rusty will make a soldier of him yet.

programme.title: Nikhil & Jay
programme.desc: Nikhil and Jay want it to rain. But they don’t just want normal rain, they want a monsoon - like their grandparents in Chennai have.

programme.title: Sarah & Duck
programme.desc: Animation. Sarah and her best friend Duck embark on simple but exciting adventures, exploring the world both near and far in their own wobbly and imaginative way. Sarah and Duck invite some friends over for a sleepover, but getting to sleep is tougher than planned.

programme.title: Charlie and Lola
programme.desc: Lola is going to Lotta's house for her first ever sleepover, and it couldn't be more exciting. But, little by little, Lola realises everything is a bit different from her normal bedtime. Lotta watches ponies on TV, not pirates like Charlie. And Lotta brushes her teeth after bath time, not before! Even a midnight feast can't cheer Lola up. When it's finally time to put the light out, Lola admits she wants to go home. Then she teaches Lotta how to play I Went to the Moon, and it turns out that falling asleep is easier than she thought.

programme.title: Moon and Me
programme.desc: Inside the little Toy House, all the friends are reading books together and thinking of their favourite stories. Colly Wobble's favourite story is a silly song about a 'Horsey in the House'! Who can resist joining in?

programme.title: BeddyByes
programme.desc: MeMo and BaBa hear a beautiful sound and wonder where it’s coming from. They head to the Play Tree, where they choose some pan pipes to play with. One of the pipes sounds like the beautiful sound, and when they play that note, the sound replies. They don’t find the source at Yummy Time, although they hear the sound again. On the Lullaby Lake, they discover that Elewhale is making the lovely noise.

programme.title: In the Night Garden
programme.desc: Igglepiggle is dancing in the garden when he loses his blanket. It has fallen on top of the teeny-tiny Pontipine house. Mr Pontipine repeatedly rings Igglepiggle on the trubliphone until, at last, Igglepiggle comes to where the blanket has fallen. Igglepiggle is thrilled to have his blanket back, the Pontipines can see out of the window again, and everyone is happy.

programme.desc: The shadow of a monster causes panic among the Piris, apart from Nugget, who is keen to investigate a new mystery. She finally tracks down the creature, but is all exactly as it seems?

programme.title: Rafi the Wishing Wizard
programme.desc: At the playground, Khia won’t let Rafi and Ruby have a turn on the zip line. Rafi makes a wish for a magical new zip line that loops through the clouds and zooms around the park. At first, it’s amazing. But Rafi and Ruby ride again and again, forgetting the rule of one turn each. Soon, a long queue forms, and the friends realise they’re doing exactly what Khia did. Rafi decides it’s time to let others have a go. She realises that playground fun works best when everyone gets a turn.

programme.title: Big Lizard
programme.desc: When a pack of pesky, migrating trilobites overrun the ship, Big Lizard has to use a hidden talent to lure them away. But one little trilobite, Rex, decides to stay.

programme.title: Spidey and His Amazing Friends
programme.desc: Spidey teams up with Thing. Spidey's tech is taken.

programme.title: Octonauts: Above & Beyond
programme.desc: While collecting pictures, Dashi and Shellington get trapped in a flooding cave.

programme.title: Knee High Spies
programme.desc: Silver Paw invades the playhouse. Jeremy and Deena must stop it from becoming her lair.

programme.title: The Weasy Family
programme.desc: The ducklings can't get their pop's attention - he spends all his time playing on his phone! They force him outside to play ball, but Weasy is obsessed. The ducklings decide to confiscate the phone, but Weasy has no intention of giving in.

programme.title: Talking Tom Heroes: Suddenly Super
programme.desc: Ginger discovers the Peak City Heroes' big secret.

programme.title: Monster Makes
programme.desc: Rebecca and Murphi are dealing with a glut of carrots from the vegetable patch, and they have made everything from carrot cake to carrot juice. This inspires Murphi’s first idea – a carton bunny rabbit. The Mini Monsters are making colourful caterpillars, and Rebecca’s uncle is snug as a bug in his woolly cardigan when he calls her on the Magic Monster Mirror. The Recycling Express brings an empty box, which Rebecca and Murphi transform into a cardboard kitty cat.

programme.title: My World Kitchen
programme.desc: Je'nae is cooking her favourite meal of Jamaican saltfish and cabbage. Her family are Jamaican, and in Jamaica saltfish and cabbage is a very popular meal. Lots of people eat it for their breakfast, but Je'nae is cooking it as a very special dinner for her friends. She is using saltfish, fresh cabbage and colourful peppers in her meal. Je'nae's friends have mixed opinions about the taste of fresh green pepper. She hopes that they will like it cooked in her recipe. Her mum has cooked some tasty Jamaican dumplings and rice to eat with the fish, and Je'nae is really looking forward to seeing if her friends will like it as much as she does.

programme.title: Hamza Loves Animals: Africa
programme.desc: Kipekee the baby elephant and her friends find ways to cool down in the hot sun. Hamza sees vultures in the wild, and some of the animals get weighed at the orphanage.

programme.title: Down on the Farm
programme.desc: Storm visits a farm in Warwickshire to find out all about some unusual animals - buffalo. JB goes to a rooftop farm in the city to discover how fish help to grow salad leaves and herbs. Some school children in London show Storm how to make compost with some very helpful creatures. JB shares a spring poem and we see how potatoes are planted on a farm in Scotland.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: It's Evie and Doug's first playdate together with their friends. They try out their new ball pit, but Waffle can't join in because he's not toilet trained. He finds fun elsewhere.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Duggee is cleaning the clubhouse, so the Squirrels take refuge in the treehouse, but it's getting a little bit cramped these days. Norrie has an idea - maybe they need to add an extension, just like her dad does when she gets new siblings.

programme.title: Octonauts
programme.desc: The Octonauts roam the oceans in search of adventure and fun. When the Octopod breaks down, Tweak and the crew search for a missing part aboard an abandoned prototype of the ship, not realising something lives there.

programme.title: Vida the Vet
programme.desc: Vida and Popcorn's search for a mysterious stink in the koala family home leads to young Pippen receiving a much-needed lesson in flossing.

programme.title: Go Jetters
programme.desc: Grandmaster Glitch demands the Grimbots find somewhere with no cars so he can practice riding his bike without stabilisers. He arrives in Venice and is delighted to find the 'streets' are empty. With a splash, he discovers there are no cars because there are no streets in this city of canals and demands the Grimbots build him some roads. The Go Jetters and other tourists now find their gondola rides blocked by roads and concrete.

programme.title: Big Lizard
programme.desc: Dad drops an essential gizmo in a hard-to-reach place. Big Lizard takes them on an underwater adventure to meet Ammon, the tentacled solution to their problem!

programme.title: Yukee
programme.desc: Stripes has borrowed Twinkle's xylophone, but he has lost it - and right before her performance! The gang race around the garden, listening for clues. But will they find it in time?

programme.title: Froglets
programme.desc: Ziff, Pipp and Button get creative with empty toilet rolls and turn into Froggie robots.

programme.title: Mr Tumble
programme.desc: It’s time to sing and sign along with Mr Tumble! Sing and sign along with Mr Tumble about being brave, friends, sharing and manners.

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Ben meets Gabe at the park for some den building and hide-and-seek. Mr Tumble and Grandad are playing hide-and-seek too - by mistake! There is a treasure hunt in the spotty surprise. Featuring signs for the words tree, hiding and magnifying glass.

programme.title: Dog Squad
programme.desc: Dan the border collie is a search and rescue dog who works with his owner Jamie. His super nose follows scents and smells so they can rescue people who need their help. A local artist is painting the view of Woofton from a hill. But when the wind gets too strong, he gets lost on his way down. Dan and Jamie are called to try to find him. Dan finds the artist's scent, leading him to his painting. Jamie recognises the scene and takes the lead, but the weather is getting worse. Can Dan's super nose lead them to the artist in time?

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: Ginger and the Peas embark on an underground chase in pursuit of a burrowing Aritchokus.

programme.title: Zog
programme.desc: Zog and the doctors do their best to care for Twiggy until his demands become too much. Once they realise what is really wrong, they help Twiggy feel special again.

programme.title: The Game Catchers
programme.desc: The Game Catchers are a team of five friends on an interstellar journey to explore fantastic planets, with the aim of learning about and playing new games. The discovered games are collected into a database to make sure they are never lost.

programme.title: Roots and Fruits
programme.desc: Live from the Roots and Fruits theatre, it’s the fabulous Avocados singing an operatic piece in their three unique voices!

programme.title: Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Oona, Baba and May visit Mossy in the Undergrowth. They discover that a mysterious visitor has been sleeping in his den - and everyone else's dens too! When Oona spots a clue, the friends set out to follow the trail and investigate. Can Detective Oona solve the case and find the culprit?

programme.title: Numberblocks
programme.desc: The toys in Numberblock Five's new toy library are all mixed up! How can Numberblock Two find something to play with? Luckily, their new friend, Sorty the Super Sorter, helps them discover that toys can be sorted by type, colour, shape and size. It’s easy to see them all and find the perfect toy when they are sorted neatly into categories.

programme.title: Colourblocks
programme.desc: Green stages a magic show to introduce her new friends Black and White. Learn the difference between light, bright and dark colours with the Colourblocks.

programme.title: Froglets
programme.desc: The Froglets find a magnifying glass and become detectives to hunt for a missing crayon.

programme.title: Monster Makes
programme.desc: It's picnic day! Rebecca and Murphi create a 'soup-er' fly in a bowl of soup. On the Recycling Express, an old storage tub becomes a totally terrific tub drum kit.

programme.title: Go Wild
programme.desc: Steve and Aneeshwar meet some agile gibbons who show them how well they can move. Though the gibbons are a little quiet, Steve and Aneeshwar have a go at showing what they sound like in the wild. Next, they meet a tall, long-legged bird called a seriema who is very interested in a pretend toy snake, before they reveal the unusual wild connection between the two animals.

programme.title: Playtime Towers
programme.desc: It’s party time in Playtime Towers, and Bella and Lift enjoy a wibbly-wobbly jelly treat. Over in Boxtropolis, this gives Sketch an idea to paint a jellyfish.

programme.title: Yukee
programme.desc: As everyone huddles in Sonny’s caravan during a storm, Toad admits he’s frightened of the sound. Can Yukee find a way to use the pitter-pitter-pitter-patter of the rain to calm him?

programme.title: Tiny Tunes
programme.desc: Lisa and the children paint calming mobiles, learning British Sign Language signs for mama, buy and cry, then sing and sign Hush Little Baby Don’t You Cry.

programme.title: Nick Cope's Popcast
programme.desc: A scaly little visitor gives Nick and Norman an idea for today’s Popcast Song.

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: Ginger and the baby Pea-Rexes search for honeysuckles, leaving behind a trail of berries.

programme.title: Piripenguins
programme.desc: A sales rep visits. Despite Pancake’s doubts, he convinces the Piris to buy extra flippers. The penguins discover that their purchases are duds but find a clever new use for them.

programme.title: Zog
programme.desc: The doctors visit Fifi and see that she is feeling sad because her pies aren’t up to her usual standard. They take her out to cheer her up - until Zog realises what she really needs.

programme.title: Rafi the Wishing Wizard
programme.desc: Rafi and Finn find a lost baby sparrow in the park. Wanting to help, Rafi wishes she could talk to animals. Suddenly, ants, squirrels and Teacup the dog begin to chatter at once, making things more confusing! Rafi realises that listening can be more important than talking. She and Finn close their eyes and hear the sparrow’s mummy calling. Guided by the sound, they find the nest and reunite the chick with its family.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Jack’s the new dog at school and the newest recruit in Rusty’s army. Jack struggles with following instructions and always forgets his hat, but Rusty will make a soldier of him yet.

programme.title: Nikhil & Jay
programme.desc: Nikhil and Jay want it to rain. But they don’t just want normal rain, they want a monsoon - like their grandparents in Chennai have.

programme.title: Sarah & Duck
programme.desc: Animation. Sarah and her best friend Duck embark on simple but exciting adventures, exploring the world both near and far in their own wobbly and imaginative way. Sarah and Duck invite some friends over for a sleepover, but getting to sleep is tougher than planned.

programme.title: Charlie and Lola
programme.desc: Lola is going to Lotta's house for her first ever sleepover, and it couldn't be more exciting. But, little by little, Lola realises everything is a bit different from her normal bedtime. Lotta watches ponies on TV, not pirates like Charlie. And Lotta brushes her teeth after bath time, not before! Even a midnight feast can't cheer Lola up. When it's finally time to put the light out, Lola admits she wants to go home. Then she teaches Lotta how to play I Went to the Moon, and it turns out that falling asleep is easier than she thought.

One of the pipes sounds like the beautiful sound, and when they play that note, the sound replies. They don’t find the source at Yummy Time, although they hear the sound again. On the Lullaby Lake, they discover that Elewhale is making the lovely noise.

programme.desc: Igglepiggle is dancing in the garden when he loses his blanket. It has fallen on top of the teeny-tiny Pontipine house. Igglepiggle is thrilled to have his blanket back, the Pontipines can see out of the window again, and everyone is happy.

programme.title: Fern Britton: Inside the Vet's
programme.desc: Fern Britton returns to The Grove Vets in Bristol for an insight into the running of a busy practice at the heart of the local community. Led by husband and wife duo Andy and Amy Valenzia, along with Dr James Greenwood and their dedicated nurses, the team do all they can to keep the clinic's 3500 patients healthy and happy. Today's fluffy clients include a Romanian rescue dog with a lump in his mouth, a floppy-eared Doberman with a sore paw, and a pair of lively Cavalier King Charles Spaniel sisters who are due to be spayed. Fern lends a hand in the much-needed grooming of a long-haired cat, and James pays a visit to a dedicated rehabilitation centre for orphaned seal pups.

programme.title: Love Your Garden
programme.desc: Alan Titchmarsh and his team are in the Wirral to create a jungle-inspired space for Conrad and Pauline Toohey, who have dedicated their lives to helping others - including severely disabled son Keiron - but whose garden is so overgrown that some of the family haven't used it for decades. Alan transforms the bottom of the garden into a tranquil retreat with a pond to attract wildlife and covered pergola surrounded by tropical planting, Katie Rushworth creates a new seating area complete with calming water feature and some really personal planting, and David Domoney builds a new viewing deck to bring the whole family back into the garden, wrapping them in fragrant textured planting to delight all the senses. Meanwhile, Frances Tophill is in Cornwall to visit the UK's only outdoor jungle at the spectacular Lost Gardens of Heligan, where she helps head gardener Cindy plant some pond lilies.

programme.title: Long Lost Family
programme.desc: In this special episode, Long Lost Family takes on the cases of women affected by a historic scandal of babies stolen at birth in Spain. Among the thousands of recent applicants to Long Lost Family was Ruth, whose first child was born in Spain in 1992 - she told the team that she believed for 19 years that her daughter had died before suspicions came to light that my daughter may not have died and was stolen at birth. At the same time, Maria Elena - a Spanish woman living in London - approached the team on behalf of her 93-year-old mother Ana as they believed that Ana's twin babies born in Madrid in 1958 may have been stolen at birth. What these women have in common is the conviction that they were victims of a scandalous practice in Spain where it is believed babies were taken from parents at birth and given or sold to other families from the beginning of the Franco dictatorship in the 1930s and continuing long after Franco's death into the early 1990s.

programme.title: Long Lost Family
programme.desc: In this special episode, Long Lost Family takes on the cases of women affected by a historic scandal of babies stolen at birth in Spain. Among the thousands of recent applicants to Long Lost Family was Ruth, whose first child was born in Spain in 1992 - she told the team that she believed for 19 years that her daughter had died before suspicions came to light that my daughter may not have died and was stolen at birth. At the same time, Maria Elena - a Spanish woman living in London - approached the team on behalf of her 93-year-old mother Ana as they believed that Ana's twin babies born in Madrid in 1958 may have been stolen at birth. What these women have in common is the conviction that they were victims of a scandalous practice in Spain where it is believed babies were taken from parents at birth and given or sold to other families from the beginning of the Franco dictatorship in the 1930s and continuing long after Franco's death into the early 1990s.

programme.title: Long Lost Family
programme.desc: In this special episode, Long Lost Family takes on the cases of women affected by a historic scandal of babies stolen at birth in Spain. Among the thousands of recent applicants to Long Lost Family was Ruth, whose first child was born in Spain in 1992 - she told the team that she believed for 19 years that her daughter had died before suspicions came to light that my daughter may not have died and was stolen at birth. At the same time, Maria Elena - a Spanish woman living in London - approached the team on behalf of her 93-year-old mother Ana as they believed that Ana's twin babies born in Madrid in 1958 may have been stolen at birth. What these women have in common is the conviction that they were victims of a scandalous practice in Spain where it is believed babies were taken from parents at birth and given or sold to other families from the beginning of the Franco dictatorship in the 1930s and continuing long after Franco's death into the early 1990s.

programme.title: Fern Britton: Inside the Vet's
programme.desc: Fern Britton returns to The Grove Vets in Bristol for an insight into the running of a busy practice at the heart of the local community. Led by husband and wife duo Andy and Amy Valenzia, along with Dr James Greenwood and their dedicated nurses, the team do all they can to keep the clinic's 3500 patients healthy and happy. Today's fluffy clients include a Romanian rescue dog with a lump in his mouth, a floppy-eared Doberman with a sore paw, and a pair of lively Cavalier King Charles Spaniel sisters who are due to be spayed. Fern lends a hand in the much-needed grooming of a long-haired cat, and James pays a visit to a dedicated rehabilitation centre for orphaned seal pups.

programme.title: Love Your Garden
programme.desc: Alan Titchmarsh and his team are in the Wirral to create a jungle-inspired space for Conrad and Pauline Toohey, who have dedicated their lives to helping others - including severely disabled son Keiron - but whose garden is so overgrown that some of the family haven't used it for decades. Alan transforms the bottom of the garden into a tranquil retreat with a pond to attract wildlife and covered pergola surrounded by tropical planting, Katie Rushworth creates a new seating area complete with calming water feature and some really personal planting, and David Domoney builds a new viewing deck to bring the whole family back into the garden, wrapping them in fragrant textured planting to delight all the senses. Meanwhile, Frances Tophill is in Cornwall to visit the UK's only outdoor jungle at the spectacular Lost Gardens of Heligan, where she helps head gardener Cindy plant some pond lilies.

programme.title: Long Lost Family
programme.desc: In this special episode, Long Lost Family takes on the cases of women affected by a historic scandal of babies stolen at birth in Spain. Among the thousands of recent applicants to Long Lost Family was Ruth, whose first child was born in Spain in 1992 - she told the team that she believed for 19 years that her daughter had died before suspicions came to light that my daughter may not have died and was stolen at birth. At the same time, Maria Elena - a Spanish woman living in London - approached the team on behalf of her 93-year-old mother Ana as they believed that Ana's twin babies born in Madrid in 1958 may have been stolen at birth. What these women have in common is the conviction that they were victims of a scandalous practice in Spain where it is believed babies were taken from parents at birth and given or sold to other families from the beginning of the Franco dictatorship in the 1930s and continuing long after Franco's death into the early 1990s.

programme.desc: Fern Britton returns to The Grove Vets in Bristol for an insight into the running of a busy practice at the heart of the local community. Led by husband and wife duo Andy and Amy Valenzia, along with Dr James Greenwood and their dedicated nurses, the team do all they can to keep the clinic's 3500 patients healthy and happy. Fern lends a hand in the much-needed grooming of a long-haired cat, and James pays a visit to a dedicated rehabilitation centre for orphaned seal pups.

programme.title: Love Your Garden
programme.desc: Alan Titchmarsh and his team are in the Wirral to create a jungle-inspired space for Conrad and Pauline Toohey, who have dedicated their lives to helping others - including severely disabled son Keiron - but whose garden is so overgrown that some of the family haven't used it for decades. Alan transforms the bottom of the garden into a tranquil retreat with a pond to attract wildlife and covered pergola surrounded by tropical planting, Katie Rushworth creates a new seating area complete with calming water feature and some really personal planting, and David Domoney builds a new viewing deck to bring the whole family back into the garden, wrapping them in fragrant textured planting to delight all the senses. Meanwhile, Frances Tophill is in Cornwall to visit the UK's only outdoor jungle at the spectacular Lost Gardens of Heligan, where she helps head gardener Cindy plant some pond lilies.
